title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
claim: From one input image and a camera path, our model generates long, coherent videos while building a persistent geometric memory.
layout: 2 stacked scene blocks; input and trajectory left, 8-frame grid right
description: The figure has two stacked blocks, one indoor and one outdoor. Each block has a left column with the input image above a colored camera-trajectory plot. The trajectory runs from black through red, orange, green, blue and purple. To its right is a 2x4 grid of generated frames, each with a colored title box such as Frame 8, Frame 100 or Frame 326. The box colors follow the trajectory colors. Every frame has a small inset in the bottom-right corner. The inset shows a gray 3D plane pool with the current view frustum highlighted in rainbow colors. Across the frames, the plane map grows to cover more of the scene. The indoor block shows a cluttered gift shop with shelves. The outdoor block shows a garden with a large inscribed stone. The eye goes first to the photographic frames, then to the insets.
caption: Given a single input image and a camera trajectory, \method autoregressively generates video while accumulating a persistent plane-based 3D memory. We show two DL3DV scenes (indoor, outdoor) with generated frames at selected indices. Insets visualize the plane pool at each frame, colored by the current view frustum. The plane geometry grows to cover the full explored scene, serving as persistent spatial memory for subsequent generation.
abstract: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives as its persistent 3D memory. PPMem augments a video diffusion transformer with a planar prediction head and a Depth Token Fusion (DTF) module: each autoregressive chunk jointly produces RGB video and planar geometry, which merges into a persistent plane memory that conditions subsequent chunks via rendered depth. The resulting memory is three orders of magnitude more compact than per-pixel point clouds (~100K primitives, 5MB for a full scene), geometrically explicit (metric depth, normals, exportable surfaces), cross-view consistent (jointly predicted by the shared backbone), and adaptive (refined by the merging procedure as generation proceeds). On DL3DV and RealEstate10K, PPMem outperforms prior 3D-grounded world models in video quality while jointly producing metric-scale depth, surface normals, and exportable planar geometry, sustaining coherence across hundreds of frames under large viewpoint changes. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/ppmem.
